# **some-moyasar: Production-Grade Rust SDK, Microkernel Architecture, and Webhook Verification Engine for the Moyasar API**

some-moyasar is an idiomatic, memory-safe, asynchronous Rust client and cryptographic webhook verification engine for the **Moyasar API** (https\://api.moyasar.com/v1)1. Engineered with the structural ergonomics of the official [stripe-node](https://github.com/stripe/stripe-node) SDK2 and tailored for high-concurrency backend systems such as Actix-web, Axum, and Tonic gRPC microservices4, the crate enforces compile-time type safety, zero data races (Send \+ Sync), and constant-time cryptographic verification.  
Built on a **microkernel architecture** driven by granular Cargo feature flags, some-moyasar allows applications to compile an ultra-lightweight core HTTP and authentication kernel while selectively opting into advanced resource namespaces. These optional domain modules span polymorphic payments, two-step payment intents, and recurring card tokenization to marketplace split settlements, SARIE and IPS bulk payouts, standalone 3D Secure authentication, and Stripe-compatible subscription refund orchestrators5. Furthermore, some-moyasar is architected as a foundational provider crate within the unified **some-payments** multi-gateway ecosystem alongside some-stripe and some-paymob10.

## **Architectural Vision and Microkernel Design**

Modern payment infrastructure requires a delicate balance between binary footprint, compile-time speed, and comprehensive domain coverage. In stripe-node, a central Stripe client dynamically instantiates and attaches resource namespaces (stripe.customers, stripe.billing.meters, stripe.webhooks) over a shared StripeResource base class and RequestSender transport layer2. Translating this pattern idiomatically into Rust without incurring monolithic compile times requires a **microkernel pattern** where the core client owns only the connection pool, authentication credentials, idempotency middleware, and error deserialization pipeline, while domain services attach as zero-cost wrapper types gated behind Cargo features.  
![][image1]

### **Core Microkernel Responsibilities (default / core)**

The microkernel base (MoyasarClient) encapsulates five cross-cutting protocol invariants dictated by the Moyasar v1 specification. Following the stripe-node resource namespace convention—where resource classes extend StripeResource and attach dynamically to the client instance2—each service accessor on MoyasarClient (client.payments().create(...), client.payment\_intents().fulfill(...), client.payouts().create\_bulk(...))8 returns a lightweight, borrow-checked wrapper struct PaymentsService\<'a\>(&'a MoyasarClient) that compiles down to a single pointer dereference with zero heap allocation.  
Authentication across the microkernel enforces a strict compile-time boundary between public and secret credentials. Moyasar authenticates requests via HTTP Basic Auth where the API key (sk\_test\_..., sk\_live\_..., pk\_test\_..., pk\_live\_...) serves as the username and the password remains an empty string (""), transmitted on the wire as Authorization: Basic base64("{api\_key}:")13. Because Moyasar strictly enforces key-type permissions—restricting publishable keys (pk\_...) to client-originated operations (POST /v1/payments, POST /v1/payment\_intents/:id/fulfill, POST /v1/tokens, and GET /v1/applepay/initiate) while requiring secret keys (sk\_...) for backend operations and returning 403 Forbidden if a publishable key attempts to read a PaymentIntent containing a client\_secret6—the microkernel encodes key types at the Rust type-system level (SecretKey versus PublishableKey). Secret key material is wrapped in secrecy::SecretString (ZeroizeOnDrop) so credentials are wiped from memory on drop and never leaked in Debug logs or crash dumps.  
Idempotency handling within the microkernel diverges fundamentally from Stripe's header-driven model. Whereas Stripe transmits idempotency tokens via an Idempotency-Key HTTP header18, Moyasar implements idempotency exclusively inside the JSON request body via the given\_id attribute, requiring a client-generated UUID (version 4 recommended)19. Furthermore, Moyasar assigns the exact UUID provided in given\_id as the primary id of the resulting Payment object19. If a network timeout or 5xx error occurs, retrying the request with the same given\_id returns the exact initial response (initiated, paid, or failed) without re-executing the charge, whereas reusing a given\_id for a different payment payload yields an HTTP 400 client-side error with the message "Payment is already created."19. Consequently, the some-moyasar microkernel automatically injects a deterministic or UUIDv4 given\_id into mutating payment payloads and enables automatic exponential backoff retries exclusively on network disruptions, open/read/write timeouts, and 5xx server responses19.  
The transport layer also normalizes polymorphic request serialization and non-standard HTTP verb semantics. While standard Moyasar endpoints accept application/json or application/x-www-form-urlencoded with bracket notation (metadata\[order\_id\]=1000)20, Moyasar's Apple Pay Web Merchant session endpoint (/v1/applepay/initiate) is documented as accepting a JSON payload inside a GET request body alongside POST form requests17, and invoice cancellation utilizes PUT /v1/invoices/:id/cancel rather than POST or DELETE23. Finally, when requests fail, the microkernel's error pipeline coerces HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, and 5xx payloads into a strongly typed MoyasarError enum capturing top-level error classifications (invalid\_request, invalid\_request\_error, authentication\_error, api\_error, record\_not\_found, intent\_not\_cancelable), field-level validation arrays (errors), two-digit ISO 8583 acquirer response codes (response\_code, where "00" denotes issuer approval), and 3D Secure authentication failure reasons8.

## **Complete Moyasar Services and API Specification**

A comprehensive examination of the Moyasar documentation hierarchy reveals **9 distinct API service domains** encompassing **37 REST endpoints**, **20 regulated payout purpose classifications**, and **11 webhook event types**8. Across these 37 endpoints, authentication boundaries heavily favor backend secret keys (sk\_), isolating publishable keys (pk\_) to exactly 4 client-facing origination routes across Payments, Payment Intents, Tokens, and Apple Pay6.  
![][image2]

### **1\. Payments Service (payments feature)**

The PaymentsService (client.payments()) is the primary transaction engine of the SDK, interfacing with /v1/payments27. It supports both single-step **Purchase** flows—which authorize and capture funds in one atomic step to reach the paid status—and two-step **Authorization** flows configured via manual: true on card or digital wallet sources, which place a hold on the cardholder's funds (authorized) until the merchant explicitly captures or voids the transaction24. Every Payment response includes both integer monetary fields in the currency's smallest unit (amount, fee, refunded, captured) and pre-formatted human-readable strings (amount\_format, fee\_format, refunded\_format, captured\_format), alongside payer ip (IPv4 collected from the originating connection), invoice\_id, callback\_url, metadata, and timestamps (created\_at, updated\_at, captured\_at, refunded\_at, voided\_at)20.

| SDK Method (client.payments()) | HTTP Method & Path | Auth Key | Request Parameters / Body | Response Type & Status Transitions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| .create(params) | POST /v1/payments | sk\_ or pk\_ | amount (int32, required), currency (ISO-4217, default "SAR"), description, callback\_url, given\_id (UUIDv4), source (polymorphic enum), metadata, splits (marketplace array), sender (AFT)19 | Payment (initiated, paid, authorized, failed, verified, expired)5 |
| .retrieve(id) / .fetch(id) | GET /v1/payments/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid)27 | Payment27 |
| .list(params) | GET /v1/payments | sk\_ | Query: page, id, status, created\[gt\], created\[lt\], metadata\[key\]20 | PaginatedList\<Payment\>44 |
| .update(id, params) | PUT /v1/payments/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid); Body: description, metadata (empty string unsets key)20 | Payment27 |
| .refund(id, amount\_opt) | POST /v1/payments/:id/refund | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid); Body: { "amount": Option\<u64\> } (omitting body refunds full charged/captured amount)5 | Payment (transitions paid or captured ![][image3] refunded)39 |
| .capture(id, amount\_opt) | POST /v1/payments/:id/capture | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid); Body: { "amount": Option\<u64\> } (full or partial capture of held funds)27 | Payment (transitions authorized ![][image3] captured)39 |
| .void(id) | POST /v1/payments/:id/void | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid); No request body required27 | Payment (transitions authorized, paid, or captured ![][image3] voided)39 |
| .verify\_stc\_otp(url, otp) | POST {transaction\_url} | pk\_ or sk\_ | Path/Query from source.transaction\_url (/v1/stc\_pays/:id/proceed?otp\_token=...); Body: { "otp\_value": String }28 | Payment (transitions initiated ![][image3] paid or failed)42 |

#### **Marketplace Payment Splits & Account Funding Transactions (AFT)**

For aggregation and facilitation platforms, POST /v1/payments accepts a splits array where each PaymentSplit entry specifies a non-zero integer amount, a recipient\_type (Entity, Platform, or Beneficiary), a recipient\_id (Uuid), an optional reference (![][image4] characters, persisted into settlement files), an optional description (![][image4] characters), a boolean fee\_source flag indicating which split absorbs Moyasar's processing fee, and a boolean refundable flag (defaulting to true) governing whether the split is reversed when the parent payment is refunded5. For Account Funding Transactions (AFT), payment creation requests also accept a sender object containing sender identification keys such as first\_name and last\_name29.

### **2\. Payment Intents Service (payment-intents feature)**

Introduced to eliminate client-side tampering in browser and mobile checkouts, the **Payment Intents API** (/v1/payment\_intents) splits payment origination across two distinct keys6. The merchant backend creates the intent using its SecretKey, locking four immutable parameters: amount, currency, description, and callback\_url6. The browser or mobile app subsequently fulfills the intent using the PublishableKey and the intent's client\_secret, supplying instrument-specific properties (source, metadata, save\_card, manual, 3ds)6. If a fulfillment request attempts to send altered values for amount, currency, description, or callback\_url, Moyasar ignores the overrides and enforces the intent's locked values6. Payments created directly from a backend server using a SecretKey—such as recurring token charges, MOTO transactions, or invoices—are already server-authorized and do not require an intent6.

| SDK Method (client.payment\_intents()) | HTTP Method & Path | Auth Key | Request Parameters / Body | Response Type & Lifecycle Rules |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| .create(params) | POST /v1/payment\_intents | sk\_ | amount (locked), currency (locked), description (locked), callback\_url (locked)6 | PaymentIntent (status: "created", client\_secret, expires\_at \= creation \+ 1 hour)15 |
| .fulfill(id, params) | POST /v1/payment\_intents/:id/fulfill | pk\_ | client\_secret, source (card, Apple Pay, Samsung Pay, STC Pay, or token), metadata, save\_card, manual, 3ds6 | Payment (returns a standard Payment object; transitions intent to fulfilled)6 |
| .retrieve(id) | GET /v1/payment\_intents/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid) (Calling with pk\_ returns HTTP 403 Forbidden)15 | PaymentIntent (includes client\_secret)15 |
| .cancel(id) | POST /v1/payment\_intents/:id/cancel | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid); No request body15 | PaymentIntent (status: "canceled"; returns 400 intent\_not\_cancelable if already fulfilled, canceled, or expired)15 |

#### **Second-Order Engineering Nuances in Intent Lifecycle & Operational Windows**

Two subtle state-machine behaviors in Moyasar's architecture require explicit compile-time and runtime safeguards in some-moyasar. First, in the Payment Intents lifecycle, fulfilled does not mean paid15. An intent tracks only whether its authorization token has been consumed (created, fulfilled, canceled), whereas the outcome of the charge itself is tracked on the resulting Payment object (GET /v1/payments/:id or payment\_paid webhook)15. Furthermore, every intent expires exactly **1 hour** after creation (expires\_at), and this window is fixed and non-configurable15. Crucially, **expiry is not a status**: an intent past expires\_at remains "status": "created" in API responses, yet calling either /fulfill or /cancel on an expired intent returns HTTP 400 Bad Request ("type": "intent\_not\_cancelable")15. To prevent backend callers from triggering spurious 400 errors, some-moyasar equips PaymentIntent with .is\_usable(\&self) \-\> bool (evaluating self.status \== IntentStatus::Created && Utc::now() \< self.expires\_at) and recommends creating intents immediately before payment submission (on\_initiating) rather than on initial page load15.  
Second, Moyasar enforces strict temporal windows across capture, void, and refund operations while exhibiting silent state retention when card issuers expire holds. On the Mada scheme, authorized payments must be captured or voided within **14 days** (whereas Visa and Mastercard permit longer scheme windows); if a merchant neither captures nor voids within that window, the issuing bank automatically releases the held funds back to the cardholder, **but Moyasar keeps the payment status as authorized and does not update it**24. For paid or captured payments, a void (POST /v1/payments/:id/void) is only permitted within approximately **2 hours** of the original transaction prior to bank settlement; once settled, funds can only be returned via a full or partial refund (POST /v1/payments/:id/refund), which requires sufficient merchant balance on live aggregation accounts39. When handling operational failures, Moyasar prescribes checking GET /v1/payments/:id and retrying once: if a void fails a second time on an authorized payment, no further action is needed because the issuer hold will expire automatically, whereas if a void fails on a paid or captured payment, the SDK automatically falls back to issuing a refund39.

### **3\. Tokenization Service (tokens feature)**

Moyasar enables recurring billing and card-on-file workflows through two complementary pathways: saving a card during a payment (source.save\_card: true on creditcard, applepay, or samsungpay) or directly tokenizing a card via /v1/tokens7. When save\_card: true is passed on a credit card charge, Moyasar returns the new token ID (source.token, prefixed with token\_) immediately in the initial initiated response—before the customer is redirected to source.transaction\_url for 3D Secure authentication—allowing the merchant backend to persist the token reference prior to redirect and activate it once the payment reaches paid46. Tokens created directly via /v1/tokens begin in initiated, transition to active once cardholder verification completes (payment\_verified), and become inactive if verification fails or when the underlying card expires30.

| SDK Method (client.tokens()) | HTTP Method & Path | Auth Key | Request Parameters / Body | Response Type & Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| .create(params) | POST /v1/tokens | pk\_ | name, number, month, year, cvc, callback\_url, save\_only (optional bool)7 | Token (id: "token\_...", status: initiated ![][image3] active after verification, or inactive on failure/expiry)30 |
| .retrieve(id) | GET /v1/tokens/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (String, e.g., "token\_...")31 | Token (masked card details for customer display)31 |
| .delete(id) | DELETE /v1/tokens/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (String)31 | () (HTTP 204 No Content empty response)31 |

### **4\. Invoices Service (invoices feature)**

The **Invoices API** (/v1/invoices) enables merchants and facilitation platforms to generate hosted e-invoices that bill customers via a Moyasar-hosted payment page24. When a customer pays an invoice using SADAD Bill, Moyasar automatically synchronizes the bill's expiration to the invoice's expiry date (capped at the 29-day SADAD provider limit) so the bill never outlives the invoice28.

| SDK Method (client.invoices()) | HTTP Method & Path | Auth Key | Request Parameters / Body | Response Type |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| .create\_bulk(params) | POST /v1/invoices/bulk | sk\_ | invoices: Vec\<CreateInvoiceParams\>32 | Vec\<Invoice\>32 |
| .retrieve(id) | GET /v1/invoices/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid)32 | Invoice32 |
| .list(params) | GET /v1/invoices | sk\_ | Query: page, id, status, created\[gt\], created\[lt\], metadata\[key\]20 | PaginatedList\<Invoice\>32 |
| .update(id, params) | PUT /v1/invoices/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid); Body: description, metadata32 | Invoice51 |
| .cancel(id) | PUT /v1/invoices/:id/cancel | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid); Uses HTTP PUT verb23 | Invoice (status transitions to canceled)23 |

### **5\. Standalone Card Authentication / 3D Secure Service (card-auth feature)**

Available for selected enterprise merchants, the **Card Authentication API** (/v1/card\_auths) decouples 3D Secure 2.x cardholder authentication from payment charging9. This allows a merchant to run standalone 3DS authentication now and charge the card later (or on another gateway) by passing source.card\_auth\_id, or to bring external 3DS MPI cryptographic parameters directly into a Moyasar payment via source.card\_auth\_data9.

| SDK Method (client.card\_auths()) | HTTP Method & Path | Auth Key | Request Parameters / Body | Response Type & Cryptographic Result |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| .create(params) | POST /v1/card\_auths | sk\_ or pk\_ | amount, currency, callback\_url, card details (number, name, month, year, cvc)9 | CardAuthentication (id: "ca\_...", transaction\_url /v1/card\_auth/:id/prepare)21 |
| .retrieve(id) | GET /v1/card\_auths/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (String, e.g., "ca\_...")21 | CardAuthentication (status: authenticated or failed; result: eci, authentication\_value, ds\_transaction\_id, version, transaction\_status, auth\_scheme, is\_frictionless)21 |

### **6\. Payouts and Payout Accounts Service (payouts feature)**

Moyasar provides a full outbound disbursement engine (/v1/payout\_accounts and /v1/payouts) capable of routing funds from a configured bank or wallet source account to Saudi bank IBANs (BankDestination) or mobile digital wallets (WalletDestination) across three settlement channels: internal, ips (Instant Payment System), and sarie (Saudi Arabian Riyal Interbank Express)8.

| SDK Method | HTTP Method & Path | Auth Key | Request Parameters / Body | Response Type & Validation Rules |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| payout\_accounts().create(p) | POST /v1/payout\_accounts | sk\_ | account\_type (bank \| wallet), properties (e.g., iban), credentials (provider private key/secrets)8 | PayoutAccount (201 Created: id, account\_type, currency, properties, created\_at)8 |
| payout\_accounts().list(p) | GET /v1/payout\_accounts | sk\_ | Query: page (default 1\)8 | PaginatedPayoutAccounts (payout\_accounts \+ meta)8 |
| payout\_accounts().retrieve(id) | GET /v1/payout\_accounts/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid)8 | PayoutAccount8 |
| payouts().create(p) | POST /v1/payouts | sk\_ | source\_id (Uuid), sequence\_number (optional 16-digit string), amount (positive int), purpose (enum of 20 values), destination (BankDestination \| WalletDestination), comment, metadata8 | Payout (201 Created: channel, status: queued, initiated, paid, failed, canceled, returned, message, failure\_reason)8 |
| payouts().create\_bulk(p) | POST /v1/payouts/bulk | sk\_ | source\_id (Uuid), payouts: Vec\<BulkPayoutEntry\>8 | BulkPayoutResponse (payouts: Vec\<Payout\>)8 |
| payouts().list(p) | GET /v1/payouts | sk\_ | Query: page (default 1\)8 | PaginatedPayouts (payouts \+ meta)8 |
| payouts().retrieve(id) | GET /v1/payouts/:id | sk\_ | Path: id (Uuid)8 | Payout8 |

Every single or bulk payout request requires a mandatory purpose classification selected from **20 regulated values** (bills\_or\_rent, expenses\_services, purchase\_assets, saving\_investment, government\_dues, money\_exchange, credit\_card\_loan, gift\_or\_reward, personal, investment\_transaction, family\_assistance, donation, payroll\_benefits, online\_purchase, hajj\_and\_umra, dividend\_payment, government\_payment, investment\_house, payment\_to\_merchant, and own\_account\_transfer)8. Encoding these 20 values into a strongly typed PayoutPurpose enum in Rust guarantees compile-time compliance with Saudi banking regulations.

### **8\. Sources (BIN Lookup) and Apple Pay Session Service (sources feature)**

The sources feature provides two pre-authorization utility services essential for custom checkout interfaces. First, the **Card Issuer & BIN Lookup** endpoint (/v1/source/issuer) inspects a card BIN (first 6 to 8 digits), full PAN, or device-payment source to return issuer\_name, issuer\_country, issuer\_card\_type (debit, credit, charge\_card, unspecified), issuer\_card\_category (e.g., Platinum, Signature), first\_digits, and last\_digits without creating a payment37. This enables merchants to dynamically distinguish local mada debit cards from international credit cards before charging the customer37. Second, the **Apple Pay Web Merchant Session** endpoint (/v1/applepay/initiate) supports Moyasar's Apple Pay Web Merchant Registration, allowing web stores to initiate signed Apple Pay sessions (merchantSessionIdentifier, nonce, merchantIdentifier, signature, operationalAnalyticsIdentifier) without needing a dedicated Apple Developer account17.

| SDK Service & Method | HTTP Method & Path | Auth Key | Request Parameters / Body | Response Type |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| sources().get\_issuer(p) | POST /v1/source/issuer | sk\_ or pk\_ | first\_digits (6–8 digits) or full card/device source37 | IssuerMetadata (issuer\_name, issuer\_country, issuer\_card\_type, issuer\_card\_category, first\_digits, last\_digits)37 |
| apple\_pay().initiate\_session(p) | GET / POST /v1/applepay/initiate | pk\_ | validation\_url, display\_name, domain\_name, publishable\_api\_key17 | ApplePayMerchantSession (epochTimestamp, expiresAt, merchantSessionIdentifier, nonce, merchantIdentifier, domainName, displayName, signature, operationalAnalyticsIdentifier, retries)17 |

### **9\. Webhooks Management API & Constant-Time Verification Engine (webhooks-api & webhook-engine)**

Moyasar provides both a REST API for programmatic webhook registration (/v1/webhooks) and real-time asynchronous event delivery governed by a 6-attempt retry schedule21.

| SDK Method (client.webhooks()) | HTTP Method & Path | Auth Key | Request / Response Details |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| .create(params) | POST /v1/webhooks | sk\_ | Body: http\_method ("post"), url, shared\_secret, events: Option\<Vec\<WebhookEventType\>\> (omitting events creates a global listener for all current and future events)21 |
| .list() | GET /v1/webhooks | sk\_ | Lists all registered webhook endpoints38 |
| .retrieve(id) | GET /v1/webhooks/:id | sk\_ | Retrieves a single webhook configuration by Uuid38 |
| .delete(id) | DELETE /v1/webhooks/:id | sk\_ | Deletes a registered webhook endpoint38 |
| .available\_events() | GET /v1/webhooks/available\_events | sk\_ | Returns the canonical list of supported webhook events21 |
| .list\_attempts(params) | GET /v1/webhooks/attempts | sk\_ | Lists webhook delivery attempts and HTTP response statuses38 |
| .retrieve\_attempt(id) | GET /v1/webhooks/attempts/:id | sk\_ | Fetches payload and diagnostic details for a specific delivery attempt38 |

#### **Cryptographic Security Analysis of the Webhook Engine**

A fundamental architectural divergence separates Stripe's webhook signing mechanism from Moyasar's webhook authentication protocol. Stripe calculates an HMAC-SHA256 signature over {timestamp}.{raw\_body} using the endpoint's signing secret and transmits the digest in the Stripe-Signature HTTP header (t=...,v1=...)53. By contrast, Moyasar embeds the consumer-assigned shared\_secret directly inside the JSON webhook payload under the secret\_token attribute alongside id, type, created\_at, account\_name, live, and data21.  
If an application validates event.secret\_token \== expected\_secret using standard string equality (==), the comparison short-circuits at the first mismatched byte, creating a timing side-channel that allows remote attackers to reconstruct the secret\_token byte-by-byte. Even if a developer applies subtle::ConstantTimeEq directly to the raw byte slices (a.as\_bytes().ct\_eq(b.as\_bytes())), slice equality returns false immediately when the slice lengths differ, leaking the exact byte length of the merchant's shared\_secret. To guarantee **strict constant-time verification with zero length leakage**, some-moyasar's ConstantTimeSecretVerifier hashes both the incoming secret\_token and the configured shared\_secret through **HMAC-SHA256** using a domain-separation key to yield two fixed 32-byte digests, and then compares those 32-byte arrays using subtle::ConstantTimeEq::ct\_eq.  
Beyond cryptographic verification, the webhook engine resolves two critical operational hazards in Moyasar's delivery pipeline. First, Moyasar's documentation exhibits a spelling discrepancy for failed payment events: GET /v1/webhooks/available\_events and the Create Webhook guide return "payment\_failed", whereas the Webhook Reference specification table documents "payment\_faild" (omitting the 'e')21. In addition, SADAD Bill documentation introduces "payment\_expired" alongside "payment\_abandoned"21. some-moyasar annotates WebhookEventType::PaymentFailed with \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_failed", alias \= "payment\_faild")\] and includes all 11 event variants so deserialization never fails in production. Second, if a recipient endpoint fails to return a 2xx status code promptly, Moyasar retries delivery 5 additional times (Attempt 1: immediate ![][image3] wait 1m; Attempt 2: \+1m ![][image3] wait 10m; Attempt 3: \+10m ![][image3] wait 30m; Attempt 4: \+30m ![][image3] wait 1h; Attempt 5: \+1h ![][image3] wait 2h; Attempt 6: \+2h ![][image3] message dropped), spanning a total window of **3 hours and 41 minutes**21. Because enforcing a naive 5-minute age tolerance on created\_at (as in stripe-node55) would reject valid late retry attempts 3 through 6, some-moyasar defaults its timestamp tolerance to 4 hours while providing a pluggable WebhookDeduplicator trait keyed by event.id (Uuid).

## **Bridging the Stripe-Parity Gap: Refunds, Customers, and Subscriptions (stripe-compat feature)**

Developers accustomed to stripe-node or building cross-gateway workflows in some-payments expect dedicated top-level services for refunds, customers, and subscriptions, including **subscription refunds**40. Because Moyasar exposes foundational primitives (POST /v1/payments/:id/refund and /v1/tokens) rather than standalone /v1/refunds or /v1/subscriptions state machines31, some-moyasar bridges this gap through the stripe-compat feature flag.

| Stripe Concept (stripe-node) | Native Moyasar Primitive | some-moyasar (stripe-compat Feature) Ergonomic Implementation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| stripe.refunds.create({ payment\_intent, amount }) | POST /v1/payments/:id/refund ({ "amount": 2000 })39 | client.refunds().create(RefundCreateParams) calls POST /v1/payments/:id/refund, validates status \== Refunded, and returns a synthesized RefundReceipt struct containing payment\_id, refunded\_amount, refunded\_format, refunded\_at, and split reversal flags5. |
| stripe.customers.create() & paymentMethods.attach() | POST /v1/tokens or save\_card: true on POST /v1/payments16 | client.customers() provides a pluggable CustomerVault trait (compatible with PostgreSQL, Redis, and Moka caches)4 that binds a merchant customer\_id to active Moyasar token\_... IDs and injects metadata\["customer\_id"\] into all charges20. |
| stripe.subscriptions.create() & Recurring Billing | Off-session POST /v1/payments with source: { type: "token", token: "token\_..." }6 | client.subscriptions() orchestrates recurring billing cycles using saved active tokens with automatic given\_id idempotency derived deterministically via Uuid::new\_v5(\&NAMESPACE, "{sub\_id}:{cycle\_index}") to guarantee **zero double-billing** across distributed worker retries19. |
| **Subscription Refunds** (Full, Partial, or Pro-Rata Unused Time) | POST /v1/payments/:id/refund with calculated partial amount39 | client.subscriptions().refund\_cycle(...) locates the cycle's Payment, computes exact pro-rata unused halalas/cents: ![][image7] and executes POST /v1/payments/:id/refund, automatically falling back to POST /v1/payments/:id/void if a full cancellation occurs within the \~2-hour unsettled void window39. |

## **Master README.md Specification for some-moyasar**

The following section provides the complete, production-ready README.md document structured for the root of the some-moyasar repository.

# **some-moyasar**

**An idiomatic, microkernel-architected Rust SDK and constant-time webhook verification engine for the Moyasar Payment Gateway API (v1).**  
Designed with the resource-namespace ergonomics of [stripe-node](https://github.com/stripe/stripe-node)2 and built to power the **some-payments** unified Rust payment ecosystem alongside some-stripe and some-paymob10.

### **Architectural Highlights**

some-moyasar combines a minimal HTTP/Auth microkernel (core) with modular feature flags (payments, payment-intents, tokens, invoices, payouts, settlements, card-auth, sources, webhooks-api, and stripe-compat), enabling applications to compile only the exact domain surfaces required for their workload14. The SDK enforces compile-time isolation between PublishableKey (pk\_...) and SecretKey (sk\_...) credentials while zeroizing secret material on drop14. Every mutating payment operation benefits from deterministic body-level idempotency via UUIDv4/v5 given\_id injection, permitting safe automated retries on network timeouts and 5xx errors without risking duplicate customer charges19. Incoming webhook payloads (secret\_token) are verified in strict constant time via double-HMAC-SHA256 and subtle::ConstantTimeEq, eliminating both timing side-channels and secret-length leakage while remaining resilient to Moyasar's payment\_faild / payment\_failed naming variance21. When the stripe-compat feature is enabled, the crate exposes top-level client.refunds(), token-backed client.customers(), and client.subscriptions() services with automated pro-rata subscription refunds and unsettled 2-hour void fallback31.

### **Core Rust SDK Implementation & Ergonomic Usage**

#### **1\. Initializing the Client & Creating a Payment with Marketplace Splits**

The MoyasarClient mirrors stripe-node ergonomics while enforcing Rust's type system across currency units, metadata limits, and idempotency keys2.

Rust  
use some\_moyasar::prelude::\*;  
use uuid::Uuid;

\#\[tokio::main\]  
async fn main() \-\> Result\<(), MoyasarError\> {  
    // Initialize the microkernel client with a SecretKey (Basic Auth with empty password)  
    let client \= MoyasarClient::builder(SecretKey::new("sk\_test\_YOUR\_SECRET\_KEY")?)  
        .max\_network\_retries(2) // Safe retries enabled via body-injected \`given\_id\`  
        .build()?;

    // Construct validated Metadata (enforces \<= 30 keys, key \<= 40 chars, val \<= 500 chars)  
    let mut metadata \= Metadata::new();  
    metadata.insert("order\_id", "ORD-2026-9941")?;  
    metadata.insert("tenant\_id", "vendor\_alpha")?;

    // Create a payment with saved token and marketplace splits  
    let create\_params \= CreatePaymentParams::builder()  
        .given\_id(Uuid::new\_v4()) // Idempotency key & resulting Payment ID  
        .amount(15000)            // 150.00 SAR in halalas (smallest currency unit)  
        .currency(Currency::SAR)  
        .description("Annual Pro Plan \+ Vendor Split")  
        .callback\_url("https\://merchant.example/payments/callback")  
        .source(PaymentSourceRequest::Token {  
            token: "token\_qbmmXzo97AESrZLS6KpWvof6uK2hAKcQGfEcKg".into(),  
            three\_ds: Some(false),  
            manual: Some(false),  
            cvc: None,  
        })  
        .splits(vec\!\[  
            PaymentSplitRequest {  
                amount: 13500,  
                recipient\_type: SplitRecipientType::Beneficiary,  
                recipient\_id: Uuid::parse\_str("3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6").unwrap(),  
                reference: Some("SPLIT-VENDOR-9941".into()),  
                description: Some("85% Vendor Revenue Share".into()),  
                fee\_source: Some(false),  
                refundable: Some(true),  
            },  
            PaymentSplitRequest {  
                amount: 1500,  
                recipient\_type: SplitRecipientType::Platform,  
                recipient\_id: Uuid::parse\_str("ae50a35c-df42-4eff-ba26-f8bc28d2af81").unwrap(),  
                reference: Some("SPLIT-PLATFORM-FEE".into()),  
                description: Some("15% Platform Commission".into()),  
                fee\_source: Some(true), // Deduct Moyasar processing fees from platform share  
                refundable: Some(true),  
            },  
        \])  
        .metadata(metadata)  
        .build();

    let payment \= client.payments().create(create\_params).await?;  
    println\!("Payment {} status: {:?} ({})", payment.id, payment.status, payment.amount\_format);  
    Ok(())  
}

#### **2\. Two-Step Payment Intents Lifecycle (Backend Creation & Expiry-Safe Inspection)**

Payment Intents lock amount, currency, description, and callback\_url on the backend before frontend card collection6.

Rust  
use some\_moyasar::prelude::\*;

async fn manage\_payment\_intent(client: \&MoyasarClient) \-\> Result\<(), MoyasarError\> {  
    // Step 1: Backend creates the intent using SecretKey  
    let intent \= client.payment\_intents().create(CreatePaymentIntentParams {  
        amount: 25000, // 250.00 SAR  
        currency: Currency::SAR,  
        description: Some("Checkout Session \#882".into()),  
        callback\_url: "https\://merchant.example/return".into(),  
    }).await?;

    // Send \`intent.id\` and \`intent.client\_secret\` to the frontend/mobile client.  
    // Later: Backend inspects the intent.  
    // Note: Moyasar keeps status \= \`Created\` even after the 1-hour \`expires\_at\` window\!  
    let fetched \= client.payment\_intents().retrieve(intent.id).await?;

    if fetched.is\_usable() {  
        // Safe to cancel because status \== Created AND Utc::now() \< fetched.expires\_at  
        let canceled \= client.payment\_intents().cancel(fetched.id).await?;  
        assert\_eq\!(canceled.status, PaymentIntentStatus::Canceled);  
    } else if fetched.status \== PaymentIntentStatus::Fulfilled {  
        // IMPORTANT: \`Fulfilled\` only means an attempt occurred, NOT that payment succeeded\!  
        // Always verify the downstream Payment status via \`client.payments().retrieve(...)\`.  
    }  
    Ok(())  
}

#### **3\. Subscription Refunds & Smart Void/Refund Routing (stripe-compat Feature)**

Because Moyasar permits voiding paid or captured payments within \~2 hours of transaction creation (before settlement) and requires POST /v1/payments/:id/refund thereafter39, some-moyasar automates both standard payment refunds and pro-rata subscription refunds:

Rust  
use some\_moyasar::prelude::\*;  
use some\_moyasar::stripe\_compat::{RefundCreateParams, RefundStrategy, SubscriptionCycleRefundParams};  
use chrono::{Duration, Utc};  
use uuid::Uuid;

async fn process\_refunds(client: \&MoyasarClient, payment\_id: Uuid) \-\> Result\<(), MoyasarError\> {  
    // 1\. Direct Stripe-like Refund (Partial or Full)  
    let receipt \= client.refunds().create(RefundCreateParams {  
        payment\_id,  
        amount: Some(5000), // Partial refund of 50.00 SAR (None \= full refund)  
        prefer\_void\_if\_unsettled: false,  
    }).await?;  
    println\!("Refunded: {} at {:?}", receipt.refunded\_format, receipt.refunded\_at);

    // 2\. Subscription Pro-Rata Refund (e.g., customer cancels 10 days into a 30-day cycle)  
    let now \= Utc::now();  
    let sub\_refund \= client.subscriptions().refund\_cycle(SubscriptionCycleRefundParams {  
        payment\_id,  
        period\_start: now \- Duration::days(10),  
        period\_end: now \+ Duration::days(20),  
        strategy: RefundStrategy::ProRata { canceled\_at: now },  
        // If full refund is requested within \~2 hours of charge, automatically voids to save fees\!  
        smart\_void\_within\_two\_hours: true,  
    }).await?;

    println\!("Subscription reversal action: {:?}, amount: {}", sub\_refund.action, sub\_refund.amount);  
    Ok(())  
}

#### **4\. Regulated Single & Bulk Payouts (payouts Feature)**

Disbursing funds to bank IBANs or mobile wallets via /v1/payouts/bulk leverages the strongly typed PayoutPurpose and PayoutDestination enums8.

Rust  
use some\_moyasar::prelude::\*;  
use uuid::Uuid;

async fn disburse\_vendor\_payouts(client: \&MoyasarClient, source\_account\_id: Uuid) \-\> Result\<(), MoyasarError\> {  
    let bulk\_response \= client.payouts().create\_bulk(CreateBulkPayoutParams {  
        source\_id: source\_account\_id,  
        payouts: vec\!\[  
            BulkPayoutEntry {  
                sequence\_number: Some("2026110500000001".into()), // 16-digit reference  
                amount: 125000, // 1,250.00 SAR  
                purpose: PayoutPurpose::PaymentToMerchant,  
                destination: PayoutDestination::Bank {  
                    iban: "SA8430400108057386290038".into(),  
                    name: "Al-Noor Trading Est".into(),  
                    mobile: "+966501234567".into(),  
                    country: "SA".into(),  
                    city: "Riyadh".into(),  
                },  
                comment: Some("Weekly Marketplace Settlement".into()),  
                metadata: None,  
            },  
            BulkPayoutEntry {  
                sequence\_number: None, // Moyasar auto-generates 16-digit sequence\_number  
                amount: 35000,  
                purpose: PayoutPurpose::PayrollBenefits,  
                destination: PayoutDestination::Wallet {  
                    mobile: "0559876543".into(),  
                },  
                comment: Some("Courier Bonus".into()),  
                metadata: None,  
            },  
        \],  
    }).await?;

    for payout in bulk\_response.payouts {  
        println\!("Payout {} via {:?}: {:?}", payout.id, payout.channel, payout.status);  
    }  
    Ok(())  
}

### **Constant-Time Webhook Verification Engine (webhook-engine)**

Moyasar delivers webhooks with a JSON body containing id, type, created\_at, secret\_token, account\_name, live, and data21. Endpoints must return a 2xx HTTP response immediately before executing slow downstream accounting logic; otherwise, Moyasar retries up to 5 additional times (1m, 10m, 30m, 1h, 2h) before dropping the message21.

Rust  
use some\_moyasar::webhook\_engine::{  
    WebhookEvent, WebhookEventType, WebhookError  
};  
use hmac::{Hmac, Mac};  
use sha2::Sha256;  
use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;  
use std::time::Duration;

/// Constant-time, zero-length-leakage verifier for Moyasar webhook payloads.  
pub struct ConstantTimeSecretVerifier {  
    expected\_secret\_digest: \[u8; 32\],  
    tolerance: Duration,  
}

impl ConstantTimeSecretVerifier {  
    /// Initializes the verifier by hashing the merchant's configured \`shared\_secret\`  
    /// with a fixed domain-separation key so comparisons always run on 32-byte digests.  
    pub fn new(shared\_secret: &str, tolerance: Duration) \-\> Self {  
        let expected\_secret\_digest \= Self::compute\_digest(shared\_secret.as\_bytes());  
        Self {  
            expected\_secret\_digest,  
            tolerance,  
        }  
    }

    \#\[inline\]  
    fn compute\_digest(input: &\[u8\]) \-\> \[u8; 32\] {  
        let mut mac \= Hmac::\<Sha256\>::new\_from\_slice(b"some-moyasar-webhook-domain-v1")  
            .expect("HMAC accepts keys of any size");  
        mac.update(input);  
        mac.finalize().into\_bytes().into()  
    }

    /// Parses the raw webhook JSON and verifies \`secret\_token\` in strict constant time.  
    pub fn verify\_and\_construct(&self, raw\_body: &\[u8\]) \-\> Result\<WebhookEvent, WebhookError\> {  
        let event: WebhookEvent \= serde\_json::from\_slice(raw\_body)  
            .map\_err(WebhookError::InvalidJson)?;

        let provided\_digest \= Self::compute\_digest(event.secret\_token.as\_bytes());

        // Constant-time comparison over fixed 32-byte SHA-256 digests:  
        // Leaks neither byte positions nor the length of the configured shared\_secret.  
        if provided\_digest.ct\_eq(&self.expected\_secret\_digest).unwrap\_u8() \!= 1 {  
            return Err(WebhookError::SecretMismatch);  
        }

        // Verify timestamp age against tolerance (default 4h to accommodate Moyasar's 3h41m retry schedule)  
        event.validate\_timestamp(self.tolerance)?;

        Ok(event)  
    }  
}

#### **Strongly Typed Webhook Event Definitions (Resilient to payment\_faild)**

Rust  
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};  
use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};  
use uuid::Uuid;

\#\[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)\]  
pub enum WebhookEventType {  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_paid")\]  
    PaymentPaid,  
    /// Handles both canonical \`payment\_failed\` and Moyasar's documented \`payment\_faild\` string.  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_failed", alias \= "payment\_faild")\]  
    PaymentFailed,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_refunded")\]  
    PaymentRefunded,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_voided")\]  
    PaymentVoided,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_authorized")\]  
    PaymentAuthorized,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_captured")\]  
    PaymentCaptured,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_verified")\]  
    PaymentVerified,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_abandoned")\]  
    PaymentAbandoned,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "payment\_expired")\]  
    PaymentExpired,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "card\_auth\_authenticated")\]  
    CardAuthAuthenticated,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "card\_auth\_failed")\]  
    CardAuthFailed,  
    \#\[serde(other)\]  
    Unknown,  
}

\#\[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)\]  
pub struct WebhookEvent {  
    pub id: Uuid,  
    \#\[serde(rename \= "type")\]  
    pub event\_type: WebhookEventType,  
    pub created\_at: DateTime\<Utc\>,  
    /// Redacted in custom \`Debug\` implementations to prevent accidental log exposure.  
    pub secret\_token: String,  
    pub account\_name: Option\<String\>,  
    pub live: bool,  
    pub data: serde\_json::Value, // Parsed on demand into \`Payment\` or \`CardAuthentication\`  
}

## **Cross-Gateway Interoperability: Designing for some-payments**

To ensure some-moyasar integrates seamlessly alongside some-stripe and some-paymob inside the overarching **some-payments** workspace10, the crate implements the shared provider abstraction layer (some-payments-trait feature). Because Stripe, Moyasar, and Paymob diverge significantly in their wire protocols, the table below establishes how some-moyasar normalizes Moyasar's primitives into the unified some-payments trait contract.

| Unified some-payments Concept | some-stripe (Global) | some-moyasar (Saudi Arabia / GCC) | some-paymob (Egypt / MENA) | some-moyasar Adapter Normalization Strategy |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Authentication Mechanism** | Bearer / Basic Auth (sk\_live\_...)53 | HTTP Basic Auth (sk\_live\_...:)14 | Auth Token / Secret Key (egy\_sk\_...) | Encapsulates Basic Auth header construction inside MoyasarClient14. |
| **Idempotency Transport** | HTTP Header (Idempotency-Key)18 | JSON Body (given\_id: Uuid)19 | Intention / Order Reference ID | Extracts the unified idempotency\_key from RequestOptions, hashes arbitrary strings via UUIDv5 if non-UUID, and injects into given\_id19. |
| **Two-Step Checkout Session** | PaymentIntent (client\_secret)57 | PaymentIntent (/v1/payment\_intents, client\_secret)6 | Intention API (client\_secret) | Maps PaymentGateway::create\_intent() directly to POST /v1/payment\_intents and exposes expires\_at (1h)6. |
| **Pre-Auth Capture & Void** | paymentIntents.capture / .cancel | POST /v1/payments/:id/capture & /void27 | Auth/Capture Transaction API | Routes unified release\_or\_refund() through .void() if authorized or within 2h of paid, else .refund()39. |
| **Webhook Verification** | Stripe-Signature HMAC header (t=...,v1=...)53 | JSON secret\_token field21 | Query/Header HMAC (hmac=...) | Implements UnifiedWebhookVerifier::verify(\&headers, \&raw\_body) by inspecting the JSON secret\_token via double-HMAC ConstantTimeEq21. |
| **Saved Card Tokenization** | PaymentMethod (pm\_...) \+ Customer (cus\_...)57 | Token (token\_...) via save\_card: true or /v1/tokens16 | Saved Card Token | Maps unified PaymentToken directly to Moyasar's token\_... identifier and verifies TokenStatus::Active before off-session charging31. |

Rust  
use async\_trait::async\_trait;

/// Unified trait shared across \`some-stripe\`, \`some-moyasar\`, and \`some-paymob\`  
/// inside the \`some-payments\` umbrella crate.  
\#\[async\_trait\]  
pub trait UnifiedPaymentGateway: Send \+ Sync {  
    type Error: std::error::Error \+ Send \+ Sync \+ 'static;

    async fn create\_intent(  
        &self,  
        amount\_minor: u64,  
        currency: &str,  
        description: Option\<&str\>,  
        callback\_url: &str,  
    ) \-\> Result\<UnifiedIntentResponse, Self::Error\>;

    async fn charge\_saved\_token(  
        &self,  
        amount\_minor: u64,  
        currency: &str,  
        token\_id: &str,  
        idempotency\_key: uuid::Uuid,  
    ) \-\> Result\<UnifiedChargeResponse, Self::Error\>;

    async fn refund\_or\_void(  
        &self,  
        transaction\_id: &str,  
        amount\_minor: Option\<u64\>,  
    ) \-\> Result\<UnifiedReversalResponse, Self::Error\>;

    fn verify\_webhook(  
        &self,  
        headers: \&http::HeaderMap,  
        raw\_body: &\[u8\],  
    ) \-\> Result\<UnifiedWebhookEvent, Self::Error\>;  
}

## **Implementation Roadmap and Architectural Recommendations**

Achieving production-grade reliability across some-moyasar and the broader some-payments ecosystem requires enforcing strict domain invariants at the type-system boundary. Because Moyasar uses standard Uuid identifiers for Payment, PaymentIntent, Invoice, Payout, PayoutAccount, Settlement, Transfer, InternalTransaction, and Webhook records8, while relying on prefixed strings for Token ("token\_...")46 and CardAuthentication ("ca\_...")21, the SDK should wrap each identifier in a distinct zero-cost newtype (PaymentId(Uuid), IntentId(Uuid), InvoiceId(Uuid), TokenId(String), CardAuthId(String)). This prevents developers from inadvertently passing an IntentId or InvoiceId into client.payments().retrieve(...). Simultaneously, pairing integer monetary amounts with currency exponent validation—where 1.00 SAR \= 100 (2 decimal places), 1.00 KWD \= 1000 (3 decimal places), and 1 JPY \= 1 (0 decimal places)8—eliminates off-by-10x billing defects in multi-currency checkouts8.  
For local development and continuous integration, some-moyasar should expose a test-utils feature flag modeled after stripe-mock57. This module should bundle deterministic JSON fixtures and local mock responders covering all 11 webhook event types (explicitly testing both "payment\_failed" and "payment\_faild")21, Moyasar's STC Pay sandbox mobile numbers (0515555555 for unregistered mobile, 0515555558 for exhausted OTP attempts, and 0515555559 for the 60-second cooldown error)45, SADAD sandbox biller code 007 (sandbox-اختباري)5, and ISO 8583 two-digit acquirer response codes24. Finally, because Moyasar requires webhook endpoints to return a 2xx status code prior to executing complex accounting updates21, the crate's web framework integrations for Actix-web and Axum4 should encourage an asynchronous transactional outbox pattern: verifying the payload in constant time, persisting (event.id, raw\_body) idempotently to PostgreSQL or Redis4, returning 200 OK immediately, and reconciling state transitions via background workers that re-fetch authoritative state (GET /v1/payments/:id) to remain immune to out-of-order webhook delivery21.
